The root cause of the bug was in the `escapeRegex` method of the FastDateParser class (line 310). When converting literal whitespace characters from the SimpleDateFormat pattern to a regex pattern, the method was appending `\s*+` (a possessive quantifier meaning zero or more whitespace characters) instead of a more restrictive pattern. This caused FastDateParser to be overly permissive when matching whitespace in the input string.

Specifically, when parsing the format "M E" (month followed by day name), SimpleDateFormat expects exactly one space between the two fields. However, FastDateFormat was accepting zero or more spaces due to the `\s*+` pattern. When parsing the input "3  Tue" with two spaces, SimpleDateFormat correctly rejected it, but FastDateFormat incorrectly accepted it.
